summaryZh: Duarte 研究组发展用于高能粒子碰撞的人工智能技术，以测量希格斯玻色子等基本粒子的性质和相互作用并寻找新物理。研究包括 LHC 数据分析、硬件加速机器学习和粒子物理基础模型。

evidence.quote: CMS Higgs and exotic searches Measurements of high-momentum Higgs bosons and searches for exotic new physics with the CMS experiment at the LHC. Fast machine learning Hardware-accelerated machine learning for low-latency, real-time trigger applications and high-throughput computing. Foundation models for particle physics Foundation models for event reconstruction and particle identification. Previous Next Principal investigator Javier Duarte is an Associate Professor of Physics at UC San Diego and a member of the CMS experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider . He leads a research group developing new artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for high-energy particle collisions to better measure the properties and interactions of elementary particles, like the Higgs boson , and search for new physics. Before joining UC San Diego, he was a Lederman postdoctoral fellow at Fermilab and received his Ph.D. in Physics at Caltech and his B.S. in Physics and Mathematics at MIT. Prof. Duarte has received the APS Henry Primakoff Award for Early-Career Particle Physics , Sloan Research Fellowship , RCSA Cottrell Scholar Award , DOE Early Career Award , and is a co-PI of the NSF HDR Institute for Accelerated AI Algorithms for Data-Driven Discovery . Research directions Our lab is interested in: LHC data analysis for Higgs boson and exotic new physics Hardware-accelerated machine learning for trigger and computing Foundation models for particle physics Diversity, inclusion, and social justice in physics Open positions Graduate students: see admissions requirements here , and undergraduate students: fill out the Google form here . Antiracism We are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive workspace. For resources, see the Resources tab. Contact information Office: Mayer Hall Addition 5513 (858) 246-4980 Lab: Mayer Hall Addition 5545 Mailing address: Javier Duarte University of California San Diego Department of Physics, 0319 9500 Gilman Drive La Jolla, CA 92093 Support Our work is supported by the Research Corporation For Science Advancement (RCSA) under grant #CS-CSA-2023-109, Department of Energy (DOE), Office of Science, Office of High Energy Physics under award number DE-SC0009919, and the National Science Foundation (NSF) under award numbers 2117997 (A3D3) and 2005369 (Voyager).
